newsitem.title: USA: U.N. body fails to agree on new Iraq sanctions.
newsitem.headline: U.N. body fails to agree on new Iraq sanctions.

text.p: The U.N. Security Council on Friday failed to reach a consensus on a U.S. and British co-sponsored proposal to impose new sanctions on Iraq for blocking U.N. weapons teams in June, according to U.N. diplomats.
Security Council members were expected to meet again on Saturday for further discussions on the resolution, Iraqi Ambassador Nizar Hamdoon said.
Council members China, Russia, France and Egypt are known to oppose new sanctions.
The resolution has been softened since Thursday, with the U.S. toning down some of the punitive language, according to an Arab diplomat.

The diplomat said the revised resolution calls for restrictions on travel only for members of the Iraqi military, police, and intelligence officials instead of the previous broader wording forbidding travel by all Iraqi government officials and their immediate families.

Further, the resolution waters down the language concerning regular 60-day sanctions reviews. The new draft says a decision on conducting reviews will be made after the next U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) report in October, rather than declaring an indefinite suspension of such reviews.
Diplomats said the U.S. proposals, even with the concessions, have met with stiff resistance from the Russian and Chinese delegations.
The Arab diplomat said France also "had trouble with the language in the new resolution."
Iraqi Ambassador Hamdoon said he "was pleased the Security Council has strong reservations about the resolution."

The Council last Friday issued a relatively mild statement deploring a series of incidents in which U.N. inspectors said Iraqi personnel had endangered U.N. helicopters and their crews assisting U.N. ground teams. Since then, inspectors have been turned away from three sites they attempted to visit.
